sentences.en: It was like a run on the bank.

sentences.en: Everybody in the Democratic Party was suddenly confronted with what they didn't want to admit up until then, which is that they have an 81-year-old candidate who would be 86

sentences.en: And it's very possible that he was not capable of completing this campaign in a vigorous and competitive way against Donald Trump.

sentences.en: But you did see, even publicly, people like Senator Claire McCaskill.

sentences.en: Joe Biden had one thing he had to do tonight, and he didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登今晚有一件事必须做到，但他没做到。

sentences.en: A former senator from Missouri, red state Democrat, was on MSNBC just minutes after the debate.
sentences.zh: 这位来自密苏里州的前参议员、红州民主党人，在辩论结束后几分钟就上了MSNBC节目。

sentences.en: He had one thing he had to accomplish, and that was reassure America that he was up to the job at his age.

sentences.zh: 但他今晚失败了。

sentences.en: She talked about, you know, this was a crisis.

sentences.en: That her phone was blowing up with a lot of Democrats, and she was very forthright about it.

sentences.en: I think there's a lot of people who are going to want to see him consider taking a different course now.

sentences.en: People like Van Jones, who was on CNN.
sentences.zh: 像范·琼斯这样的人，他当时在CNN上。

sentences.en: He used to work in the Obama White House.

sentences.en: We're still far from our convention, and there is time for this party to figure out a different way forward if he will allow us to do that.

sentences.en: Those are some of the public people.

sentences.en: And obviously, in the hours and days that followed, more came out and said, well, this is something we need to think about.
sentences.zh: 显然，在随后的几个小时和几天里，更多人站出来说，嗯，这是我们需要考虑的事情。

sentences.en: But the people I was talking to were people behind the scenes, people who have run White

sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，这是一个转折点，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's not just the media.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是媒体的问题。

sentences.zh: 我认为拜登竞选团队希望这只是媒体炒作。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 这些质疑来自四面八方，来自各个角落。

sentences.en: Take me through, Peter, the argument for why this poor performance meant that Biden should be replaced.
sentences.zh: 彼得，带我梳理一下，为什么这种糟糕的表现意味着拜登应该被替换？

sentences.en: How do they explain that thinking?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何解释这种想法的？

sentences.en: Well, look, what a lot of people who defended President Biden will say is that incumbent presidents don't do well in their first debate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，许多为拜登总统辩护的人会说，现任总统在第一次辩论中表现通常都不好。

sentences.en: And that is true.
sentences.zh: 这是事实。

sentences.en: Historically, that's been true.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，确实如此。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan, George W.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根、乔治·W·布什、巴拉克·奥巴马、唐纳德·特朗普，

sentences.en: Bush, Barack Obama, Donald Trump, all lost arguably their first debate when they were running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 他们在竞选连任时的第一次辩论可以说都输了。

sentences.en: But the difference is if Obama doesn't register a good performance against Mitt Romney, first of all, nobody thought that Obama wasn't capable of being president as a result.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，如果奥巴马在对阵米特·罗姆尼时表现不佳，首先，没人会因此认为奥巴马没有能力担任总统。

sentences.en: And second of all, he had another debate about a week or two later in order to try to recover.
sentences.zh: 其次，他还有大约一两周后的另一场辩论来尝试挽回局面。

sentences.en: Neither of those factors works here.
sentences.zh: 这两个因素在这里都不适用。

sentences.en: Biden's problem from this debate is much more existential, is much more profound because it's about whether he is able to perform the office of president, not just for the next
sentences.zh: 拜登这次辩论的问题更具生存意义，也更深刻，因为这关乎他是否有能力履行总统职责，不仅是未来几个月，

sentences.en: few months, but for the next four and a half years.
sentences.zh: 而是未来四年半。

sentences.en: And there's not going to be another debate until September.

sentences.en: So he doesn't have another big audience opportunity to change people's minds, to show that, in fact, he does still have it and can run the country.

sentences.en: And that's a real problem for him.
sentences.zh: 这对他是真正的问题。

sentences.en: And there's this broader context here, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这里还有一个更广泛的背景，对吧？

sentences.en: Voters have been telling pollsters for a year now that Biden's age is a major concern for them.
sentences.zh: 选民们一年来一直在告诉民调机构，拜登的年龄是他们主要关心的问题。

sentences.en: We've seen Biden's age before our very eyes.

sentences.zh: 我们看到他在演讲和公开露面时步履蹒跚。

sentences.zh: 彼得，几个月前，在调查拜登儿子亨特的特别检察官发布了那份关注拜登精神状态的报告后，我们曾和你讨论过这个问题，

sentences.en: state, in part, you know, saying that the president was, quote, a well-meaning elderly man with a poor memory and had, quote, diminished faculties in advancing age.
sentences.zh: 报告中部分提到，总统是一位“善意但记忆力不佳的老人”，并且“随着年龄增长，认知能力有所下降”。

sentences.en: But at the time, the White House dismissed that report as a partisan hit job.
sentences.zh: 但当时，白宫将那份报告斥为党派攻击。

sentences.en: So in a sense, this debate performance was the capstone of something that's been in the air for a very long time.

sentences.en: It's just that this time it was undeniable.

sentences.zh: 根本无法粉饰。

sentences.en: Biden.

sentences.zh: 但他对我说，现在同样的恐惧意味着他们再也无法支持拜登了，

sentences.en: But now that same fear, he said to me, now meant that they could no longer stand behind

sentences.en: Biden, that they worried that he had been diminishing over a period of time and that his staff and the people around him had hidden that from the public.

sentences.en: all this has raised this fundamental question for a lot of Democrats, for a lot of journalists, for voters, which is what you're getting at.
sentences.zh: 我们在辩论台上看到的那个是真实的拜登吗？白宫一直在向我们隐瞒他吗？

sentences.zh: 总统本人着手做了两件事。

sentences.en: His campaign was thrown into full-blown damage control over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 首先，私下里，他会见了捐款人并向他们保证，是的，他仍然是一位可行的候选人，他们应该继续支持他。

sentences.en: And the president himself set out to do two things.
sentences.zh: 然后公开地，他进行了一场竞选闪电战，在四个州参加了七场活动。

sentences.en: First, privately, he met with donors and assured them, yes, he's still a viable candidate and that they should still support him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他周五的第一站是北卡罗来纳州罗利市的一次集会。

sentences.en: And then publicly, he went on a campaign blitz, traveling to seven events in four states.
sentences.zh: 这在辩论前就已经安排好了，但这给了他一个机会，既能展示他能胜任这份工作，

sentences.en: And his first stop on Friday, in fact, was at a rally in Raleigh, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，北卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: This was already scheduled before the debate, but it gave him an opportunity to both show that he can do the job.
sentences.zh: 又能展示活力和生命力。

sentences.en: Thank you, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你昨晚做了什么，但我花了90分钟在台上与一个道德水平像巷子里野猫一样的家伙辩论。

sentences.en: To demonstrate vigor and vitality.
sentences.zh: 并回应他自己的表现。

sentences.en: I don't know what you did last night, but I spent 90 minutes on the stage debating a guy who has the morals of an alley cat.
sentences.zh: （注：此条对应原文第149条，因输入编号缺失，此处补齐）

sentences.en: And to address his own performance.
sentences.zh: （注：此条对应原文第149条，因输入编号缺失，此处补齐）

sentences.en: I know I'm not a young man.
sentences.zh: 我知道我不再年轻了。

sentences.en: State the obvious.
sentences.zh: 这还用说吗。

sentences.en: Well, I know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道。

sentences.en: And he says pretty candidly, he says, yeah, I'm not a young man.
sentences.zh: 他非常坦诚地说，是的，我不再年轻了。

sentences.en: I don't walk as easy as I used to.
sentences.zh: 我走路不像以前那么利索了。

sentences.en: I don't speak as smoothly as I used to.
sentences.zh: 我说话也不像以前那么顺畅了。

sentences.en: I don't debate as well as I used to.
sentences.zh: 我辩论也不像以前那么出色了。

sentences.en: But he goes on.
sentences.zh: 但他接着说。

sentences.en: Well, I know what I do know.
sentences.zh: 不过，我知道我所知道的。

sentences.en: I know how to tell the truth.
sentences.zh: 我知道如何说真话。

sentences.en: I know how to tell right from wrong.
sentences.zh: 我知道如何明辨是非。

sentences.en: I know how to do this job.
sentences.zh: 我知道如何做好这份工作。

sentences.en: I know how to get things done.
sentences.zh: 我知道如何把事情办成。

sentences.en: I know like millions of Americans know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，就像数百万美国人所知道的那样。

sentences.en: When you get knocked down, you get back up.
sentences.zh: 当你被打倒时，你要重新站起来。

sentences.en: And, you know, he comes across as pretty vigorous, pretty energetic.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他表现得相当有活力，相当有干劲。

sentences.en: Of course, he's reading from a teleprompter.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是在照着提词器念。

sentences.en: Always a lot easier to read from a teleprompter.
sentences.zh: 照着提词器念总是容易得多。

sentences.en: But I think more important than that was the body language and the spirit that he brought to the moment.
sentences.zh: 但我认为比这更重要的是他当时表现出的肢体语言和精神状态。

sentences.en: It sounds like teleprompter or not, the Biden who appears at the rally is meaningfully different, at least in style, from the president that we saw in the debate stage.
sentences.zh: 听起来不管有没有提词器，出现在集会上的拜登，至少在风格上，与我们在辩论台上看到的总统有着明显的不同。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you think this has changed anything.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否认为这改变了什么。

sentences.en: Has the conversation changed?
sentences.zh: 对话改变了吗？

sentences.en: No, not fundamentally.
sentences.zh: 不，从根本上没有。

sentences.en: I think fundamentally that people still recognize that there's an issue here.
sentences.zh: 我认为从根本上讲，人们仍然意识到这里存在一个问题。

sentences.en: Now, there was pushback among Democrats saying, okay, take a breath.
sentences.zh: 现在，民主党内部出现了反弹，说，好吧，先冷静一下。

sentences.en: Get a hold of yourself.
sentences.zh: 控制一下你自己。

sentences.en: He's not dropping out.
sentences.zh: 他不会退出的。

sentences.en: I don't think you judge a person's, the body of their work on one night.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你应该凭一个晚上来评判一个人的全部工作成果。

sentences.en: They don't always go the way you want to.
sentences.zh: 事情并不总是如你所愿。

sentences.en: I have confidence in the president because he's delivered.
sentences.zh: 我对总统有信心，因为他做出了成绩。

sentences.en: I understand that, you know, he had a raspy voice.
sentences.zh: 我理解，你知道，他的嗓音沙哑。

sentences.en: But, like, I've told folks, who cares?
sentences.zh: 但是，就像我告诉人们的那样，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: We have a choice this November between someone that's a good person, a good president with a real record of results, and someone that has brought shame on the presidency.
sentences.zh: 今年十一月，我们面临的选择是：一个是好人，一个有实实在在政绩的好总统；而另一个人则让总统职位蒙羞。

sentences.en: Don't let 90 Minutes define a career of a president who's been in office for three and a half years,
sentences.zh: 不要让90分钟的辩论定义一位在任三年半的总统的职业生涯，

sentences.en: been in politics for 50 years, and overshadow the important issues that he stands for.
sentences.zh: 他从政50年，不要让这90分钟掩盖了他所坚持的重要议题。

sentences.en: And so you heard that line of thinking in the spin room and on TV.
sentences.zh: 所以你在舆论室和电视上都听到了这种想法。

sentences.en: Look, I think Joe Biden had a bad debate night, but it doesn't change the fact that Donald Trump was a bad president.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为乔·拜登那晚辩论表现很差，但这并不能改变唐纳德·特朗普曾是一位糟糕总统的事实。

sentences.en: And by the way, Trump did terribly, too, which is a fair point.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，特朗普的表现也很糟糕，这话说得没错。

sentences.en: Trump may have been more lucid in the sense that he sounded stronger.
sentences.zh: 特朗普可能更清醒一些，因为他听起来更有力。

sentences.en: But if you actually looked at what he said, listened to what he said, he said so many things that were just not true.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细看他说了什么，听他说了什么，他说了太多根本不是事实的话。

sentences.en: And it helped Biden that former President Barack Obama put out a statement saying, hey, guys, I've seen bad debates.
sentences.zh: 前总统巴拉克·奥巴马发表声明说，嘿，伙计们，我见过糟糕的辩论，这帮到了拜登。

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Don't freak out, in effect, is what he said.
sentences.zh: 实际上他想说的是，别惊慌。

sentences.en: And Jim Clyburn.
sentences.zh: 还有吉姆·克莱伯恩。

sentences.en: And if he asked my opinion, I would give it, as I always do.
sentences.zh: 如果他征求我的意见，我会像往常一样给出我的看法。

sentences.en: Who is his very close ally in Congress from South Carolina, the congressman who helped get him the nomination in the first place, said, stay the course.
sentences.zh: 他是拜登在国会中来自南卡罗来纳州的亲密盟友，正是这位国会议员当初帮助拜登获得了提名，他说，坚持到底。

sentences.en: He should stay in this race.
sentences.zh: 他应该留在竞选中。

sentences.en: He should demonstrate going forward his capacity to lead the country.
sentences.zh: 他应该在未来证明他领导国家的能力。

sentences.en: So it was important to have those voices out there among prominent Democrats trying to calm the waters.
sentences.zh: 因此，在杰出的民主党人中发出这些声音来平息事态是很重要的。

sentences.en: But it only went so far because the waters are still churning underneath.
sentences.zh: 但这只能起到一定作用，因为水面之下依然暗流涌动。

sentences.en: Peter, I'm curious how his donors are reacting to all this.
sentences.zh: 彼得，我很好奇他的捐款人对此有何反应。

sentences.en: I mean, you mentioned that part of his full-court press is to reassure them that he's got the mental acuity to run.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提到他全力以赴的一部分工作是向他们保证他有足够的精神敏锐度来参选。

sentences.en: How successful has he been at that?
sentences.zh: 他在这方面做得有多成功？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that there's certainly some donors who are resigned.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为肯定有一些捐款人已经认命了。

sentences.en: They feel like there's not much choice.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得没得选。

sentences.en: But there are others who actually are considering jumping off the boat, jumping on what Mika Brzezinski on Morning Joe called the hysteria train.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他人正在考虑跳船，加入米卡·布热津斯基在《早安乔》节目中所说的“歇斯底里列车”。

sentences.en: And I think that it's an open question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: But part of the thing is, of course, they're waiting to see how the polls really shake out.
sentences.zh: 但部分原因当然是，他们正在等待观察民调结果到底会如何变化。

sentences.en: The initial polls after any debate are often not really representative of how an event settles into the political narrative.
sentences.zh: 任何辩论后的初步民调往往并不能真正代表一个事件如何融入政治叙事。

sentences.en: And the polling and data so far have been kind of contradictory.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，民调和数据一直有些矛盾。

sentences.en: On the one hand, it shows that Trump clearly beat Biden, that Biden clearly lost,
sentences.zh: 一方面，它显示特朗普显然击败了拜登，拜登显然输了，

sentences.en: and that Biden has only reinforced the doubts that most voters had about his age and mental capacity.
sentences.zh: 而且拜登只是加深了大多数选民对他年龄和精神能力的怀疑。

sentences.en: That's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: At the same time, there's some polling showing that the overall horse race number, who are you going to vote for, hasn't moved dramatically yet, if it does at all.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，也有一些民调显示，整体的竞选数字，即你打算投给谁，目前还没有发生剧烈变动，如果说有变动的话。

sentences.en: And that, you know, it's possible this is baked in, that people who are going to vote against him are still going to vote against him.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这可能是已经定局了，那些打算反对他的人仍然会反对他。

sentences.en: The people who are going to vote for him, holding their nose, may not be happy about it, may still be voting for him.
sentences.zh: 那些捏着鼻子打算投给他的人，可能对此并不高兴，但可能还是会投给他。

sentences.en: But there's a tell.
sentences.zh: 但有一个信号。

sentences.en: The tell was from the Biden campaign.
sentences.zh: 这个信号来自拜登竞选团队。

sentences.en: When they put out a memo by Jen O'Malley Dillon, who's his top political person at the campaign, and she says if you see polls go down in the next few days or weeks,
sentences.zh: 当他们发布了一份由竞选团队最高政治顾问珍·奥马利·狄龙撰写的备忘录时，她说如果你看到未来几天或几周民调下降，

sentences.en: what's telling is that she is, in fact, anticipating that polls would be bad for them and trying to set expectations for supporters and voters and donors saying,
sentences.zh: 说明问题的是，她实际上是在预料民调对他们不利，并试图为支持者、选民和捐款人设定预期，说，

sentences.en: don't let that panic you any further.
sentences.zh: 不要让这些让你进一步恐慌。

sentences.en: That's normal, and we'll get past that just as we have other bumps in the road.
sentences.zh: 这是正常的，我们会像克服路上的其他坎坷一样度过难关。

sentences.en: It seems like the Biden effort over the weekend has, in some sense, quieted some public doubts from key Democrats, right?
sentences.zh: 看起来拜登团队在周末的努力，在某种意义上平息了一些关键民主党人的公开质疑，对吧？

sentences.en: There's not a—we didn't see a deluge of senior lawmakers going on Sunday talk shows and saying, Mr. President, step aside.
sentences.zh: 并没有——我们没有看到大批资深议员出现在周日的谈话节目中说，总统先生，请退位。

sentences.en: But from what you're saying and based on the reporting that we've seen from our colleagues, the effort has not by any means ended the discussion about replacing Biden.
sentences.zh: 但根据你所说的以及我们同事的报道，这种努力绝没有结束关于更换拜登的讨论。

sentences.en: That is very much still happening under the surface.
sentences.zh: 这在表面之下依然非常活跃。

sentences.en: Yeah, that discussion is very much alive among Democrats.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种讨论在民主党人中非常活跃。

sentences.en: Will Biden and should Biden remain as the candidate?
sentences.zh: 拜登会，以及应该继续作为候选人吗？

sentences.en: And the question then becomes is, if he doesn't, what then?
sentences.zh: 那么问题就变成了，如果他不这样做，那会怎样？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Peter, given that this discussion of Biden stepping aside is still, as you said, very much alive,
sentences.zh: 彼得，鉴于关于拜登退选的讨论正如你所说依然非常活跃，

sentences.en: what would it look like for someone to replace him on the presidential ticket at this point in the campaign, just a few months before Election Day?
sentences.zh: 在竞选活动的这个阶段，距离选举日仅剩几个月，如果有人要取代他成为总统候选人，会是什么样子？

sentences.en: It sounds like it would be pretty daunting.
sentences.zh: 听起来这会非常艰巨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, look, we have never had a situation like this, not certainly in modern times.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，我们从未遇到过这样的情况，至少在现代历史上没有。

sentences.en: No president has ever dropped out of the race so late in the cycle.
sentences.zh: 从来没有总统在竞选周期如此晚的时候退选。

sentences.en: And you have to remember a couple things.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住几件事。

sentences.en: First of all, the Democratic National Convention, which would anoint a new nominee, is in late AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 首先，将要确定新候选人的民主党全国代表大会是在八月下旬举行。

sentences.en: But they're actually scheduled to take a roll call before the convention begins on August 7th.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上计划在8月7日大会开始前进行点名投票。

sentences.en: So that means we have five weeks between now and when the roll call is scheduled to be held to decide a nominee.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从现在到预定进行点名投票以决定候选人之间，我们只有五周时间。

sentences.en: If the president were to drop out, that would create this truncated, incredibly intense, incredibly wide open, incredibly volatile,
sentences.zh: 如果总统要退选，那将创造一场缩短的、极其激烈的、极其开放的、极其动荡的、

sentences.en: short campaign to figure out who would be the nominee.
sentences.zh: 短暂的竞选活动来确定谁将成为候选人。

sentences.en: And it's complicated logistically, it's complicated politically, it's complicated in all sorts of ways,
sentences.zh: 这在后勤上很复杂，在政治上很复杂，在各方面都很复杂，

sentences.en: and we don't really know what's going to happen or how it would happen because we've never seen it before.
sentences.zh: 而且我们真的不知道会发生什么或怎么发生，因为我们以前从未见过。

sentences.en: But it is conceivable.
sentences.zh: 但这是可以想象的。

sentences.en: It is possible.
sentences.zh: 这是可能的。

sentences.en: The president has to decide that he's not going to run.
sentences.zh: 总统必须决定他不再参选。

sentences.en: If that doesn't happen, then there's no conteSt.
sentences.zh: 如果那没有发生，那么就没有竞争。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's no way anybody sees of forcing him off the ballot if he chooses to continue to run.
sentences.zh: 如果他选择继续参选，没有人能强迫他退出选票。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be any appetite for trying to find a way to undo his nomination other than with his consent.
sentences.zh: 除了征得他的同意，似乎没有任何人有兴趣去寻找撤销他提名的方法。

sentences.en: He controls the 3,900 delegates that are going to be at the convention.
sentences.zh: 他控制着将参加大会的3900名代表。

sentences.en: They're obligated to vote for him on the first ballot.
sentences.zh: 他们有义务在第一轮投票中投给他。

sentences.en: So it has to be, first, his decision on whether he continues to run.
sentences.zh: 所以首先必须是他自己决定是否继续参选。

sentences.en: If he does, then that's it.
sentences.zh: 如果他继续，那就是这样了。

sentences.en: That's the end of that question.
sentences.zh: 那个问题就结束了。

sentences.en: But if he doesn't, then it's jump ball.
sentences.zh: 但如果他不这样做，那就是一场混战。

sentences.en: Would his replacement automatically be Kamala Harris as the vice president?
sentences.zh: 他的继任者会自动是副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: If it were after the convention and they were both nominated and then he stepped aside the last minute,
sentences.zh: 如果是在大会之后，他们都已经获得提名，然后他在最后一刻退选，

sentences.en: then they probably would simply go to Kamala Harris because she had been ratified by the convention as the vice presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 那么他们很可能会直接转向卡玛拉·哈里斯，因为她已经被大会批准为副总统候选人。

sentences.en: That's possible.
sentences.zh: 那是可能的。

sentences.en: But if we're talking about a situation before the convention, it's anybody's guess.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们谈论的是大会之前的情况，那谁也说不准。

sentences.en: There's about a dozen other prominent Democrats out there who are looking at jumping in if suddenly the nomination is up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 还有大约十几位其他杰出的民主党人，如果提名突然变得空缺，他们都在考虑加入竞争。

sentences.en: But so who are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 那么我们指的是谁呢？

sentences.en: What are some of the most prominent names that have come up?
sentences.zh: 出现过哪些最响亮的名字？

sentences.en: Well, other than Kamala Harris, you have a number of governors, particularly Gavin Newsom of California, Gretchen Whitmer of Michigan, Jamie Pritzker of Illinois.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了卡玛拉·哈里斯，还有一些州长，特别是加利福尼亚州的加文·纽森、密歇根州的格雷琴·惠特默、伊利诺伊州的杰米·普利兹克。

sentences.en: There are, of course, those who ran last time who might jump back in, in theory.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有那些上次参选的人，理论上可能会重新加入。

sentences.en: Senator Cory Booker, Senator Amy Klobuchar, potentially even maybe Pete Buttigieg, who is currently the transportation secretary.
sentences.zh: 科里·布克参议员、艾米·克洛布查尔参议员，甚至可能还有目前担任交通部长的皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: But the ones who are going to have the best chance are those who have an apparatus already, who have a set of donors and fundraisers who can raise money instantly,
sentences.zh: 但最有机会的是那些已经拥有竞选机构的人，拥有可以立即筹集资金的捐款人和筹款人的人，

sentences.en: and who have the ability to get on TV and get media attention without having to work as hard for it.
sentences.zh: 以及有能力上电视并获得媒体关注而无需为此付出太多努力的人。

sentences.en: And that does suggest, obviously, a sitting vice president or a sitting governor.
sentences.zh: 这显然暗示了现任副总统或现任州长。

sentences.en: Basically, hitting reset on the whole nomination process requires embracing a moment of genuine political chaos.
sentences.zh: 基本上，重置整个提名程序需要拥抱一个真正的政治混乱时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the theoretical downside of this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是理论上的负面影响。

sentences.en: But, of course, I mean, there's also a potential upside, right?
sentences.zh: 但当然，我的意思是，也有潜在的正面影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Massive media attention, potentially, for whoever the replacement Democrat is.
sentences.zh: 对于任何取代拜登的民主党人来说，可能会获得巨大的媒体关注。

sentences.en: The possibility that that replacement could energize a lot of Democratic voters and independents and even potentially moderate Republicans out there who dislike Trump but just couldn't get excited about Biden.
sentences.zh: 这种替代者有可能激励许多民主党选民和独立选民，甚至可能包括那些不喜欢特朗普但对拜登无法感到兴奋的温和派共和党人。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Whoever emerges will have a certain advantage of freshness, right?
sentences.zh: 无论谁脱颖而出，都会有一种新鲜感的优势，对吧？

sentences.en: And that person will have a generational argument to make against Trump because whoever it would be would be younger than Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且那个人将有一个针对特朗普的代际论点，因为无论那个人是谁，都会比特朗普年轻。

sentences.en: And suddenly Trump is then the old candidate.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，特朗普就成了那个“老候选人”。

sentences.en: He's 78.
sentences.zh: 他78岁了。

sentences.en: And that new Democratic candidate will be able to say, I'm the next generation.
sentences.zh: 而那位新的民主党候选人将能够说，我是下一代。

sentences.en: This guy is also too old to be president.
sentences.zh: 这家伙也太老了，不适合当总统。

sentences.en: And if you're concerned about our guy was, can he make it through four years, then you should be picking me because the other guy can't make it either through four years.
sentences.zh: 如果你担心我们的人能否撑过四年，那么你应该选我，因为另一个人也撑不过四年。

sentences.en: Now, the downside, of course, is these are people who are largely untested on a national stage, at least in this kind of an environment.
sentences.zh: 现在，缺点当然是，这些人大多在全国舞台上未经考验，至少在这种环境下是这样。

sentences.en: And you don't know how people will do once they actually jump in.
sentences.zh: 你不知道人们一旦真正加入竞争会表现如何。

sentences.en: They didn't have the advantage of a year-long primary contest to prove themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们没有经过长达一年的初选竞争来证明自己的优势。

sentences.en: Before you jump into a race, you can look really attractive.
sentences.zh: 在你跳进一场比赛之前，你看起来可能非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: Look at Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 看看罗恩·德桑蒂斯。

sentences.en: Before he jumped in to the Republican primaries, on the Republican side, they all thought, wow, he's really great.
sentences.zh: 在他加入共和党初选之前，在共和党那边，他们都认为，哇，他真的很棒。

sentences.en: Didn't turn out to be so great once he got on the campaign trail.
sentences.zh: 等他真正踏上竞选之路时，情况并没有那么乐观。

sentences.en: The magic didn't actually appear.
sentences.zh: 奇迹并没有真正出现。

sentences.en: So that's the danger here is we don't know which of these Democrats, if any, would have the ability to shine when the big giant collegialites are on them.
sentences.zh: 所以现在的危险在于，我们不知道这些民主党人中，如果有的话，谁有能力在聚光灯下大放异彩。

sentences.en: And we're clearly in a delicate moment right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在显然处于一个微妙的时刻。

sentences.en: But are any of these potential contenders trying to signal interest at this point?
sentences.zh: 但这些潜在的竞争者中，有人在此时试图释放出参选意向吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: It sort of seems like the art of raising your hand for something but not wanting it too publicly?
sentences.zh: 看起来就像是那种既想举手示意，又不想表现得太公开的艺术？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really good question because you obviously can't do anything that seems disloyal to Biden, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，这确实是个好问题，因为你显然不能做任何看起来对拜登不忠诚的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Nobody's willing to take on Biden directly and say, I'm now running and you should take him down.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意直接挑战拜登，说“我现在要参选，你们应该把他拉下马”。

sentences.en: So the trick here is you have to be loyal, loyal, loyal, right up to the minute that Biden says he's not running, at which point then suddenly you're off to the races.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的诀窍在于，你必须保持忠诚、忠诚、再忠诚，直到拜登宣布他不参选的那一刻，在那之后你才能突然全力以赴。

sentences.en: And doing that from a standing start is not a good idea for any campaign.
sentences.zh: 而且对于任何竞选活动来说，从零开始做这件事都不是个好主意。

sentences.en: So they have to find ways of talking to their people, lining up donors, thinking about what kind of a campaign would look like, who might be their strategist,
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须想办法与自己的人沟通，争取捐款人，思考竞选活动会是什么样子，谁可能是他们的战略家，

sentences.en: without letting anybody know that they're doing that.
sentences.zh: 同时不能让任何人知道他们在做这些事。

sentences.en: At least not let anybody in our business know that because it would obviously backlash on them.
sentences.zh: 至少不能让我们这一行的人知道，因为这显然会遭到反噬。

sentences.en: And that's a very hard thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常困难的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I've heard that there are people out there making phone calls who want to run.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我听说外面确实有人在打电话，想要参选。

sentences.en: But nobody's going to admit that outright because it would be damaging to them.
sentences.zh: 但没有人会直接承认，因为那会对他们造成损害。

sentences.en: And in terms of logistics here, I know this is all very hypothetical, but if a new candidate were to become the nominee, do they get all the money Biden raised?
sentences.zh: 就后勤方面而言，我知道这都是非常假设性的，但如果一位新候选人成为提名人，他们能得到拜登筹集的所有资金吗？

sentences.en: Do they get his campaign team or are they literally creating a presidential campaign from scratch with four months to go?
sentences.zh: 他们能接手他的竞选团队吗？还是说在距离大选仅剩四个月的情况下，他们真的要从零开始组建一个总统竞选团队？

sentences.en: I mean, presumably they would adopt a lot of Biden's apparatus.
sentences.zh: 我是说，大概他们会沿用拜登的大部分班底。

sentences.en: As for the money, a lot of the money these days is in kind of super PACs and these sort of amorphous structures that can go immediately to a different candidate.
sentences.zh: 至于资金，如今很多钱都在所谓的超级政治行动委员会（Super PACs）和那些不透明的结构中，这些钱可以立即转给另一位候选人。

sentences.en: And everybody who contributed to Biden can now contribute to the new candidate.
sentences.zh: 而且所有曾经捐给拜登的人现在都可以捐给新候选人。

sentences.en: And then Biden can still spend his money as he chooses in support of whoever the candidate is.
sentences.zh: 然后拜登仍然可以随心所欲地花他的钱来支持任何最终的候选人。

sentences.en: So there's that advantage in a way could actually increase some fundraising.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这确实是一个优势，甚至可能增加一些筹款。

sentences.en: But you're right, they would be starting from scratch in a lot of ways, at least in terms of a national organization.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对，在很多方面他们确实要从零开始，至少在全国性组织方面是这样。

sentences.en: And obviously for this to even happen, it relies on Biden's stepping aside here, as you said.
sentences.zh: 显然，这一切要发生，正如你所说，前提是拜登要退位。

sentences.en: Everything you've laid out so far suggests that he is for now at least closed off to this suggestion.
sentences.zh: 你目前所阐述的一切都表明，至少现在，他对这个建议是拒绝的。

sentences.en: And I have to ask what you think from your reporting would change that.
sentences.zh: 我必须问问你，根据你的报道，你认为什么会改变这一点。

sentences.en: Well, President Biden is a proud man.
sentences.zh: 嗯，拜登总统是个自尊心很强的人。

sentences.en: He's a stubborn man.
sentences.zh: 他是个固执的人。

sentences.en: As a lot of people of any age are, he is reluctant to confront and face his own weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 就像许多任何年龄段的人一样，他不愿面对和承认自己的弱点。

sentences.en: And he's not going to be talked out of running by a bunch of media chattering class pundits and junior Democrats.
sentences.zh: 而且他不会被一群媒体评论员和初级民主党人劝说放弃竞选。

sentences.en: I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你想想看。

sentences.en: He's been running for president since 1987.
sentences.zh: 他从1987年就开始竞选总统了。

sentences.en: And the idea that he is now in office and running the country, and as he thinks it, running it pretty well,
sentences.zh: 他现在身居高位，管理着这个国家，而且在他看来，管理得还不错，

sentences.en: that he's going to simply step aside because a bunch of people tell him he should.
sentences.zh: 他会仅仅因为一群人告诉他应该这样做就退位吗？

sentences.en: He reacts viscerally to that.
sentences.zh: 他对这种说法有本能的抵触。

sentences.en: Of course he doesn't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 当然，他不想那样做。

sentences.en: In fact, when you talk to Democrats, they're very conscious of not trying to push him because it could have the opposite reaction, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，当你和民主党人交谈时，他们非常注意不去逼他，因为这可能会产生相反的效果，对吧？

sentences.en: It could trigger him to want to stay even more.
sentences.zh: 这可能会促使他更想留下来。

sentences.en: The people who have influence with him, not that many people.
sentences.zh: 至于那些对他有影响力的人，其实没几个人。

sentences.en: I mean, at this point, he's been in politics since 1972 when he was elected to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从1972年当选参议员以来，他一直身处政坛。

sentences.en: And the people he considers his peers, most of them are gone, right?
sentences.zh: 他认为的同僚，大多数都已经不在了，对吧？

sentences.en: He's not surrounded by people whose opinion he truly respects.
sentences.zh: 他身边并没有多少他真正尊重其意见的人。

sentences.en: Obama and Clinton, the only two former presidents out there other than Jimmy Carter who are Democrats,
sentences.zh: 奥巴马和克林顿，除了吉米·卡特之外，仅有的两位在世的民主党前总统，

sentences.en: I don't know that if they told him it was time to pull the plug that he would listen to that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道如果他们告诉他该收手了，他是否会听。

sentences.en: In fact, he might, again, do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他可能又会反其道而行之。

sentences.en: He still resents Obama for discouraging from running in 2016.
sentences.zh: 他至今仍对奥巴马在2016年劝阻他参选感到不满。

sentences.en: Obviously, congressional leaders like Chuck Schumer, Nancy Pelosi, Hakeem Jeffries, Jim Clyburn,
sentences.zh: 显然，像查克·舒默、南希·佩洛西、哈基姆·杰弗里斯、吉姆·克莱伯恩这样的国会领袖，

sentences.en: people like that could have an influence if they were to go as a group to him in a way
sentences.zh: 像他们这样的人，如果能以某种方式集体去劝他，可能会有影响力，

sentences.en: like the Republicans went to Nixon in 1974 and said that, you know, he wasn't going to survive.
sentences.zh: 就像1974年共和党人去找尼克松说他撑不下去了那样。

sentences.en: Maybe that might influence him.
sentences.zh: 也许那可能会影响他。

sentences.en: But I don't think they're likely to do it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们不太可能这样做。

sentences.en: It doesn't look like they're likely to do that.
sentences.zh: 看起来他们不太可能那样做。

sentences.en: Who does have his ear?
sentences.zh: 谁能听得进他的话？

sentences.en: I mean, who does he really listen to?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他真正听谁的？

sentences.en: Who do we know he's going to be listening to in this moment?
sentences.zh: 我们知道在这一刻他会听谁的？

sentences.en: Well, the real people he listens to the most are his family, the very family-oriented guy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他真正最听的人是他的家人，他是一个非常顾家的人。

sentences.en: Remember, he went home to Wilmington almost every night when he was a senator.
sentences.zh: 记住，当他还是参议员时，他几乎每天晚上都回威尔明顿的家。

sentences.en: Even now, as president, he flies home to Wilmington most every weekend.
sentences.zh: 即使现在身为总统，他几乎每个周末也都会飞回威尔明顿。

sentences.en: And he's at Camp David this weekend with his family.
sentences.zh: 这个周末他和家人在戴维营。

sentences.en: They're there because they had already planned to be together for a photo shoot, ironically, with Annie Leibovitz.
sentences.zh: 他们在那儿是因为他们早就计划好要和安妮·莱博维茨一起拍照片，讽刺的是。

sentences.en: So the family was already gathering at Camp David, which gives him an opportunity, right?
sentences.zh: 所以家人已经在戴维营聚齐了，这给了他一个机会，对吧？

sentences.en: It gives him an opportunity to have a heart-to-heart conversation with the people who mean the most to him.
sentences.zh: 这给了他一个与对他最重要的人进行深入交谈的机会。

sentences.en: In particular, Jill Biden, of course, the first lady, his sister, Valerie, the kids and the grandkids.
sentences.zh: 特别是吉尔·拜登，当然，还有第一夫人、他的妹妹瓦莱丽、孩子们和孙辈们。

sentences.en: We don't know what that conversation looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道那场谈话是什么样子的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's as private as it comes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是极其私密的。

sentences.en: Someday there'll be histories written and memoirs written.
sentences.zh: 总有一天会有历史和回忆录写出来。

sentences.en: And I'm fascinated to read what's happening this weekend at Camp David because I think it's kind of pivotal.
sentences.zh: 我很着迷于阅读这个周末在戴维营发生的事情，因为我认为这具有某种关键意义。

sentences.en: But what we do know is that up until now, at least, Jill has been all in.
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的是，至少到目前为止，吉尔一直全力支持他。

sentences.en: She's been encouraging him to run, and it sounds like she's been encouraging him to stay in.
sentences.zh: 她一直鼓励他参选，听起来她也一直鼓励他留下来。

sentences.en: And a lot of people think her voice is the most important voice in this.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为她的声音在这件事上是最重要的。

sentences.en: And just to pause on this for a second, Peter, it sounds like you're saying something pretty remarkable, actually,
sentences.zh: 在这里暂停一下，彼得，听起来你说的这件事相当引人注目，

sentences.en: which is that this very small handful of people have influence over what is going to be a massive decision
sentences.zh: 那就是这一小撮人对一个即将做出的重大决定有影响力，

sentences.en: that affects hundreds of millions of Americans and really the entire world.
sentences.zh: 这个决定影响着数亿美国人，甚至整个世界。

sentences.en: Well, don't underplay it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不要低估它。

sentences.en: But yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 但没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: And you're right to point out the stakes here because it's not just about Joe Biden and his future.
sentences.zh: 你指出这里的利害关系是正确的，因为这不仅仅关乎乔·拜登和他的未来。

sentences.en: It is about this presidential race, and it is about whether you want Donald Trump back in office.
sentences.zh: 这关乎这场总统竞选，也关乎你是否想让唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫。

sentences.en: That's the way most Democrats look at it.
sentences.zh: 大多数民主党人都是这样看的。

sentences.en: And the difference between a Biden presidency and a Trump presidency is about as stark as you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统任期和特朗普总统任期之间的差异，是你所能想象到的最鲜明的对比。

sentences.en: And this will have consequences that will ripple out for years to come.
sentences.zh: 这将产生波及未来多年的后果。

sentences.en: Peter, I kind of want to end where we began this conversation, which is with this question of Democrats' mindset right now post-debate
sentences.zh: 彼得，我想回到我们谈话的起点，也就是关于辩论后民主党人心态的问题，

sentences.en: and the question of what's motivating them in this moment.
sentences.zh: 以及是什么在这一刻激励着他们的问题。

sentences.en: Privately, they're talking about replacing Biden.
sentences.zh: 私下里，他们正在讨论替换拜登。

sentences.en: They seem too scared to do that publicly for all the reasons we've discussed, including that the White House is basically telling them to stop talking about it
sentences.zh: 他们似乎太害怕公开这样做，原因正如我们所讨论的，包括白宫基本上在告诉他们停止谈论这件事，

sentences.en: and that Biden probably won't step aside anyway, so all of this may just be useless hand-wringing.
sentences.zh: 而且拜登可能无论如何都不会退位，所以这一切可能只是徒劳的焦虑。

sentences.en: And all of that raises a pretty essential question for me, which is, are Democrats about to recommit to a damaged nominee who had a disastrous debate,
sentences.zh: 所有这些对我来说提出了一个非常核心的问题，那就是，民主党人是否要因为对拜登总统的忠诚，而重新承诺支持一位在辩论中表现灾难性、已经受损的提名人，

sentences.en: who may only get worse over time, out of loyalty to President Biden?
sentences.zh: 一位随着时间推移可能会变得更糟的提名人？

sentences.en: Or do you think on some level they really believe this is all just overblown, that it's one debate, everybody has bad days, and Biden really can recover from all this?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为在某种程度上，他们真的相信这一切只是被夸大了，这只是一场辩论，每个人都有状态不好的时候，拜登真的能从这一切中恢复过来？

sentences.en: I think there's a lot of doubt in the party that he can really recover from this.
sentences.zh: 我认为党内有很多人怀疑他能否真正从中恢复过来。

sentences.en: It is the argument, obviously, that Biden campaign is making, and it's really the only argument they have available to them to say, look, don't overreact here.
sentences.zh: 这显然是拜登竞选团队正在提出的论点，这也是他们唯一能用的论点，即“看，别反应过度”。

sentences.en: It's just the media hyperventilating.
sentences.zh: 这只是媒体在过度惊慌。

sentences.en: We will recover like we've recovered before.
sentences.zh: 我们会像以前一样恢复过来。

sentences.en: And it is what they have to say because they don't have anything else that they can say.
sentences.zh: 这是他们必须说的话，因为他们没有其他话可说。

sentences.en: But almost every Democrat outside of the inner circle that I talk to
sentences.zh: 但几乎我交谈过的每一个核心圈子之外的民主党人，

sentences.en: Biden says this was a complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 拜登说这是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: They are not sugarcoating it.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有粉饰太平。

sentences.en: They saw what they saw with their own eyes, and they think that it's not tenable for the campaign to pretend otherwise.
sentences.zh: 他们亲眼所见，他们认为竞选团队假装没发生过是站不住脚的。

sentences.en: And it's particularly devastating because the weakness of the Biden campaign has always been concerns about his age.
sentences.zh: 这尤其具有破坏性，因为拜登竞选团队的弱点一直是对他年龄的担忧。

sentences.en: People have expressed that to pollsters and in interviews with reporters going back more than a year.
sentences.zh: 人们在一年多前就向民调机构和记者采访中表达过这一点。

sentences.en: And now they just saw it for themselves on TV in their living rooms, more than 50 million of them.
sentences.zh: 现在，超过5000万人在电视上亲眼看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And to convince them not to believe what they saw with their own eyes is just a monumental task politically.
